turns.ask: how do I update everything from git and rebuild?
activity: model route opus Opus: operations procedure ("update everything")
turns.answer:
Short answer: there's probably nothing new to pull right now, but your install looks damaged, so do a full rebuild anyway. I can't run any of this myself. You run the commands in a cmd window, outside the UI.

What I found (as of the last fetch, today at 05:52 UTC):
- PianoidCore, PianoidBasic and PianoidTunner are all on dev with no local changes. Each is 0 commits behind, so they're up to date. They're also 2 to 4 commits ahead, meaning you have local commits that aren't pushed.
- PianoidInstall is on the branch feature/dev-6b34-assistant-ops-knowledge, not master. It's 9 commits ahead and 0 behind, with no local changes.
- Your engine (pianoidCuda) was built on 2026-10-15. I can't tell whether it needs a rebuild because the git history doesn't go back that far.
- Problem: pip left half-removed folders in the venv: ~andas, ~atplotlib, ~ianoidcuda-0.1.0.dist-info and ~ianoidcuda_debug-0.1.0.dist-info. That means an uninstall stopped partway, usually because a file was locked. pandas, matplotlib or the engine itself may be broken.

Steps (in cmd, root folder D:\repos\wt-6b34-install):

1. Update PianoidInstall itself (docs, scripts, the assistant):
   git -C D:\repos\wt-6b34-install pull --ff-only
   This pulls your current feature branch, not master. If you want master, switch to it first. If tools\pianoid-assistant\package.json or package-lock.json changed, run npm install in tools\pianoid-assistant, then restart the assistant with the Start assistant button.

2. Update the three sub-repos and rebuild what changed:
   cd /d D:\repos\wt-6b34-install
   update-repos.bat
   It pulls Core, Basic and Tunner with --ff-only and rebuilds only what changed (by default both the release and debug engines). It stops the backend before a CUDA build. Leave the window in front; a CUDA build takes 5 to 15 minutes.

3. Because of the half-removed packages, force a full rebuild even if nothing was pulled:
   - First make sure nothing holds the engine file: close the Pianoid window, then check with
     tasklist /M pianoidCuda.cp312-win_amd64.pyd
     tasklist /M pianoidCuda_debug.cp312-win_amd64.pyd
     Neither should list a python process.
   - Then:
     cd /d D:\repos\wt-6b34-install\PianoidCore
     build_pianoid_basic.bat
     build_pianoid_cuda.bat --heavy --both
   Always pass --both. Use the scripts inside PianoidCore, not the old copies at the root of the repo. Don't wrap the build in vcvars64.bat. Wait for "[SUCCESS] Build completed." (the log is PianoidCore\build.log).
   - If pandas or matplotlib still fail to import afterwards, reinstall them in PianoidCore\.venv, for example:
     .venv\Scripts\python -m pip install --force-reinstall pandas matplotlib
     That's my suggestion, not a documented step. Don't do this for pianoid_cuda: always rebuild the engine with the build script.

4. Check, in PianoidCore:
   .venv\Scripts\python -c "import pianoidCuda; print(pianoidCuda.__file__)"
   The path it prints must be inside PianoidCore\.venv.
   .venv\Scripts\python -c "import pianoidCuda_debug"
   Run this as its own command. Then start Pianoid and click APPLY: the status should turn green with no traceback in the backend log. After that I can confirm the new engine build time from here.

If you see "Access is denied" or "File is locked" during the build, something still holds the engine file. Close it and rerun the heavy build.

Docs: http://localhost:8001/guides/OPERATIONS_FOR_ASSISTANT/#update and http://localhost:8001/guides/OPERATIONS_FOR_ASSISTANT/#rebuild

turns.ask: the launcher is stuck at start, what do I do?
activity: model route opus Opus: bug analysis ("stuck")
turns.answer:
Since you're chatting with me, the launcher and the assistant service are already running. So "stuck" means one of two things, and I can only see the second.

What I checked:
- The backend (the synthesis engine) is not running: no process, nothing answering on port 5000. No preset is loaded, so the app can't play anything yet.
- The modal adapter isn't running either. You only need it for modal extraction.
- I also can't see an open Pianoid UI tab right now.
- Your installed builds look current. Your repos are not behind (as of the last fetch, 05:52 today), and nothing says the Basic package or the frontend needs a rebuild or reinstall. The engine check couldn't be completed, but I found no sign that an update broke things.

Case 1: the start window is stuck before the UI appears
Tell me the last line it shows. The usual causes:
- "Checking for updates": this can take up to 8 seconds per repo. Just wait.
- A pop-up hidden behind other windows. If one says the stack is already running, it cancels after 30 seconds. A CUDA warning continues on its own after 30 seconds. Check the taskbar.
- A Windows admin prompt (UAC) for the GPU clock lock, waiting on the taskbar. Accept it. If you decline, the launch continues anyway.
- "Updates accepted - running update-repos.bat": a build is running. This takes 5 to 15 minutes, so let it finish.
- "Press any key": either a plain run or an error. Read the text above that line and send it to me.

Case 2: the UI is up but nothing happens after you click APPLY
- Check the backend log: D:\repos\wt-6b34-install\PianoidCore\logs\backend_stdout.log. A line starting with "[launcher ...] killed PID(s)" means the launcher stopped the process; it didn't crash.
- If the log says "Address already in use", an old backend is still holding the port. In PowerShell, in D:\repos\wt-6b34-install, run:
  powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\kill_pianoid.ps1
  Then click APPLY again.
- I can also start the backend from here (you'll be asked to confirm). After that you still need to load a preset in the UI.

Two things that won't cause a stuck start:
- PianoidInstall has 3 uncommitted file changes and is on a feature branch, not master. That only matters for the next update, because the update script pulls the current branch.
- Some leftover folders from an earlier pip uninstall are harmless.

Guide: http://localhost:8001/guides/OPERATIONS_FOR_ASSISTANT/#symptoms

What does the start window show last, or did you already click APPLY?

turns.ask: what do I need to install on a new machine?
activity: model route opus Opus: operations procedure ("install")
turns.answer:
The setup scripts install almost everything. You only need to provide the basics first and then run four steps in order. I can't run any of this for you; you run it on the new machine.

Before you start
- Windows 10 or later, 64-bit.
- An NVIDIA GPU of compute capability 7.5 or newer (an RTX 2060 or newer).
- Git. If it's missing, run install-git.bat as Admin.
- You install these two yourself; the scripts don't:
  - the NVIDIA display driver
  - an ASIO audio driver for your sound card

Step 1: get the code (cmd, in any parent folder)
  git clone https://github.com/DSPianoid/PianoidInstall
  cd PianoidInstall
  clone-packages.bat
This puts PianoidTunner, PianoidCore and PianoidBasic (the dev branch) inside PianoidInstall.

Step 2: system packages (right-click setup-packages.bat in PianoidInstall, Run as administrator, choose 1)
It installs:
- Python 3.12
- the Visual Studio 2022 C++ Build Tools
- CUDA Toolkit 12.6
- SDL2 to C:\SDL2-2.30.8
- SDL3 to C:\SDL3-3.1.6
- Node.js 20
Restart Windows if it asks, which can happen after Visual Studio or CUDA. Option 7 in the same menu reinstalls the NVIDIA display driver; it reboots the machine.

Step 3: build everything (cmd, NOT as Admin, in PianoidInstall)
  setup-pianoid.bat
This sets up Python and its packages, builds the engine and installs the UI packages. It takes 5 to 15 minutes. The build output goes to PianoidCore\build.log.

Step 4: assistant dependencies (cmd). Step 3 does not do this.
  cd PianoidInstall\tools\pianoid-assistant
  npm install
Without it the launcher won't start the assistant. After that there is a one-time login.

Optional
- Desktop shortcut: double-click make-shortcut.bat.
- Local docs server, in PianoidInstall:
  pip install mkdocs mkdocs-material
  mkdocs serve -a localhost:8001

Check that it works (cmd, in PianoidCore)
  .venv\Scripts\python -c "import pianoidCuda; print('OK')"
  .venv\Scripts\python -c "import Pianoid; print('OK')"
Then start Pianoid, click APPLY (the status should turn green) and play a key.

Guide: http://localhost:8001/guides/OPERATIONS_FOR_ASSISTANT/#new-machine
First-run checklist: http://localhost:8001/guides/STARTUP_TROUBLESHOOTING/#first-run-checklist

Want me to look up the details of the assistant login?

turns.ask: the UI is up but APPLY says the address is already in use
activity: model route opus Opus: sticky follow-up (1 of 2 after an Opus turn)
turns.answer:
Something else is holding port 5000. The launcher isn't running a backend (it has no backend process), and nothing on 5000 answers as a Pianoid backend. Most likely an old backend process from an earlier session or the update was left behind. I can't kill processes, so you'll need to do this part.

1. Clear the stale process. Open a cmd window anywhere and run:
   curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/kill-stale
   This only kills whatever is listening on ports 5000 and 5001. The UI, the launcher and I keep running.

2. Click APPLY again.

If it still says the address is in use, something else may be on the port:
- In cmd, run: netstat -ano | findstr :5000
- The last number on the LISTENING line is the process ID (PID). Look it up in Task Manager (Details tab, PID column).
- If it's an old python process from Pianoid, end it there.
- If it's another program, close that program, or change its port if you can.

Don't use tools\kill_pianoid.ps1 for this. It stops the whole stack, including the UI, the launcher and me, so it's only for starting over.

Once APPLY works, tell me and I'll check that the engine is healthy and on the new build.

Docs: http://localhost:8001/guides/OPERATIONS_FOR_ASSISTANT/#symptoms (see also Port Conflicts in STARTUP_TROUBLESHOOTING)
